newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey plans milling, durum wheat import tax rise.
newsitem.headline: Turkey plans milling, durum wheat import tax rise.

text.p: The Turkish government is planning a further rise in the milling and durum wheat import taxes, which were already increased late in June, to divert users to domestic crop, a government official said on Friday.
"The rates will be raised again. The final decision will be made by the government," said the official.
"The proposed new rates are around 40 percent for durum wheat and 45 percent for milling wheat," he told Reuters.

The former Islamist-led government raised import taxes on milling wheat, durum wheat, corn and feed barley to 35 percent, 30 percent, 35 percent and 20 percent, respectively, on June 30. The rates prior to that date was 15 percent for all the grains.

Traders said the move to further raise the rates was linked to plans by the Turkish Grain Board (TMO), the government's grain buyer, to buy up to 2.2 million tonnes of wheat from farmers in 1997/98, up from 650,000 tonnes a year ago.
"The government wants the millers and pasta producers to use local crop as much as possible," said a trader of a Western grain company based in Turkey.
Officials said the TMO had bought 1.36 million tonnes of wheat and some 950,000 tonnes of barley from the new crop from farmers as of Thursday.
